alignments.note: Interrogative הֲ takes the fronted question auxiliary *Will* under rule 17; the verb keeps its subject pronoun and lexical rendering.

נָשָׂא פָּנִים 'lift the face' rendered *show partiality*: an idiom rendered by words of its own, writing neither morpheme's lexeme, so fused under rules 6/30 as הֵשִׁיב פָּנִים → deny. *ye* is the finite verb's subject pronoun (rule 17); *to* is the preposition the English verb needs to reach the suffix's *him* and joins the verb's rendering under rule 44. Target head on *partiality* by rule 44's light-verb subtraction. Source head on the first token s002 under rule 6's deterministic fallback for an idiom whose rendering writes no morpheme's lexeme (the same reading JOB.13.10 takes); the competing reading is rule 23's governing verb s004.
3ms suffix on פָּנֶה realized as the object pronoun *him* in the ASV's recasting (rule 18).
אִם opening the second member of a disjunctive question takes the fronted auxiliary *Will* under rule 17; the ASV writes no *Or* for it, so no connective competes for the particle.
Assimilated article on אֵל; the ASV writes bare *God* with no *the*, so unrepresented under rule 12.
Finite verb takes its subject pronoun and lexical verb *ye contend* (rule 17); the fronted *Will* is the אִם particle's.

review_notes: Two parallel yes/no questions: הֲ takes the first *Will* and אִם the second under rule 17.

נָשָׂא פָּנִים → *show partiality* fused as noncompositional; source head moved to the first token s002 under rule 6's fallback for an idiom rendered by a word of its own, with the governing verb s004 named as the alternative.
